top_news.title: AI Search - AI Search now supports GLM-5.3 Flash
top_news.dek: Cloudflare's AI Search now supports the GLM-5.3 Flash model on Workers AI.
top_news.brief: Cloudflare has integrated GLM-5.3 Flash into its AI Search service. The model features a 1,048,576-token context window, allowing for extensive document processing and retrieval tasks within the Workers AI ecosystem.

top_news.title: DAMP: Decay-Aware Mixed-Precision Recurrent-State Quantization
top_news.dek: DAMP introduces post-training quantization for recurrent states in Gated DeltaNet and Kimi Delta Attention to reduce memory usage and decoding latency.
top_news.brief: Recurrent states in models like GDN and KDA are typically stored in FP32, leading to high memory consumption and bandwidth bottlenecks. DAMP (Decay-Aware Mixed-Precision) addresses this by applying post-training quantization to these states, optimizing memory footprint without significantly sacrificing performance.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing recurrent state quantization process

top_news.title: Cloudflare Extends AI Search to Make it Easier for Agents and Developers to Search Custom Data
top_news.dek: Cloudflare has expanded its AI Search service to provide developers and agents with integrated, multimodal search capabilities over custom datasets.
top_news.brief: Cloudflare AI Search is designed as a managed retrieval service that simplifies the integration of custom data into AI agents. It supports multimodal search and is built to work natively within the Cloudflare ecosystem, reducing the complexity of setting up search infrastructure for AI applications.

top_news.title: Superagent
top_news.dek: Superagent provides a platform for managing and deploying AI agents.
top_news.brief: Superagent serves as a centralized hub for developers to build, host, and manage AI agents. The platform focuses on simplifying the agent lifecycle, from initial configuration to deployment and monitoring.

primary.title: DAMP: Decay-Aware Mixed-Precision Recurrent-State Quantization
primary.summary: Softmax attention stores key and value vectors for every preceding token, causing inference memory to grow with sequence length. Recent language models incorporating Gated DeltaNet (GDN) or Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) reduce this cost by replacing the KV cache in most layers with fixed-size recurrent states. However, these recurrent states are commonly stored in FP32 and consume substantial GPU memory; their updates are memory-bandwidth bound and contribute significantly to decoding latency. To our knowledge, we are the first to study post-training quantization of recurrent states in GDN and KD

primary.title: Marginal Coverage Credit Reduces Redundant Exploration in Parallel State-Entropy Optimization
primary.summary: Policy Gradient for Parallel State Entropy maximization (PGPSE) expands state-space coverage by training independently parameterized policies in replicated copies of the same environment. However, its pooled team-entropy score measures only collective exploration and cannot identify policies that contribute non-redundant coverage. We introduce Marginal Coverage Credit for PGPSE (MCC-PGPSE), which combines leave-one-policy-out coverage with state-owner specialization to estimate policy-specific credit. MCC-PGPSE preserves PGPSE's pooled objective and redistributes non-negative auxiliary intrins

primary.title: AI agents have no sense of time and are not aware of it
primary.summary: AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Codex have no sense of time, according to a new study. Both systematically overestimate how long tasks will take. Codex is off by as much as ten times the actual duration. They also rate their own work about 20 percentage points too high. For long, autonomous tasks, that creates a real problem with oversight.
